title: Treating Graves' hyperthyroidism
summary: Control symptoms, then pick a definitive therapy with the patient.

expansion: PTU only in: 1st trimester, thyroid storm, minor reaction to methimazole (refusing RAI/surgery)

next.content: After the 1st trimester, methimazole is used
Relapse? RAI or surgery preferred over a 2nd ATD course
Most become hypothyroid: start levothyroxine when FT4 falls

cards.text: Fever or sore throat: stop drug, check WBC + diff
Older/cardiac: methimazole first, stop 2–3 days before RAI
Methimazole to euthyroid, then iodide 10–14 days

cards.trapReason: The ATA and FDA recommend against PTU as first-line therapy because of severe hepatotoxicity. Exceptions: 1st trimester, thyroid storm, methimazole intolerance.
Iodide given before RAI blocks the gland's uptake of the radioactive iodine. If used, give it 3–7 days after RAI.
β-Blockers should be tapered slowly; abrupt withdrawal may incite a thyroid storm.

s-bb.explanation: β-Blockade is recommended in all symptomatic thyrotoxicosis, especially in older adults, resting HR > 90, or cardiovascular disease. It controls symptoms but doesn't fix the cause.

s-ptu.explanation: In the 1st trimester, the risk of methimazole embryopathy outweighs PTU hepatotoxicity, so PTU is preferred.

s-mmi.explanation: Methimazole should be used in virtually every patient who chooses ATD therapy. Response takes 4–6 weeks, which is why the β-blocker comes first.

s-duration.explanation: To induce remission, continue ATDs for at least 12–24 months. Average remission is about 40%–50%; longer courses do better.

s-agranulo.explanation: Agranulocytosis is rare but serious, usually in the first 3 months. Patients should stop the drug and get a WBC with differential at fever or sore throat.

s-rai-no.explanation: Pregnancy is an absolute contraindication. Lactating patients and those planning pregnancy within 6 months should also avoid RAI.

s-rai-pre.explanation: Hormone levels rise briefly after RAI, so older and cardiac patients are often pretreated with methimazole. Stop it 2–3 days before and restart 3–7 days after.

s-surg-1.explanation: Surgery should be strongly considered for a large gland (≥ 80 g) or severe ophthalmopathy (also suspected cancer or primary hyperparathyroidism needing surgery).

s-surg-2.explanation: Surgery should be strongly considered for a large gland (≥ 80 g) or severe ophthalmopathy (also suspected cancer or primary hyperparathyroidism needing surgery). RAI can worsen eye disease.

s-surg-prep.explanation: Give methimazole until biochemically euthyroid (usually 6–8 weeks), then add iodide for 10–14 days to reduce gland vascularity.
